about: Programmes and funds, each with its access routes and its heat relevance (explicit, related or potential). A programme is not an open call. Schema and rules: README.md.

records.name: Nexa Lighthouse (climate and health innovation, Asia and the Pacific)

remit.text: Funds proven climate and health innovations in Asia and the Pacific that help health actors act on climate-risk signals, with extreme heat one of its hazards.

relevance.label: explicit
relevance.why: Extreme heat is named as one of the hazards the call addresses.

access_note.text: Applications go through Grand Challenges Canada's Fluxx portal during an open call.

recipients.text: Organisations; individuals cannot apply.

geography.text: Implementation in eligible countries in Asia and the Pacific listed in the call's Appendix B.

records.name: Nexa (climate and health, Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean)

remit.text: Climate and health innovation in Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, including extreme heat.

relevance.label: explicit
relevance.why: Heat is one of the hazards the programme covers; its 2026 call was for Africa, Latin America and the Caribbean, not Asia.

recipients.text: Organisations; implementation in eligible countries outside Asia.

remit.text: Grants for climate action and biodiversity projects in ODA-eligible countries, led by organisations based in Germany with local partners.

relevance.label: potential
relevance.why: Adaptation has been one of the call's themes; whether a heat project fits a given year's priorities needs confirming in that year's funding announcement.

access_note.text: Annual call; the lead must be established in Germany and partner with local organisations.

recipients.text: Non-profit organisations based in Germany, with one or two local implementing partners.

remit.text: Grants of 60,000 to 200,000 euros for local non-profit organisations in ODA-eligible countries working on climate and biodiversity.

relevance.label: potential
relevance.why: A local adaptation project could address heat; the call's themes are climate and biodiversity in general, so fit needs confirming.

access_note.text: Annual call with an eligibility check first, then a full proposal for those invited.

recipients.text: Sub-national, national and regional non-profit organisations in ODA-eligible countries.

records.name: APN Collaborative Regional Research (CRRP) and Scientific Capacity Development (CAPaBLE)

remit.text: Annual calls for regional research and capacity development on global change in Asia and the Pacific.

relevance.label: potential
relevance.why: Climate risk and health research in Asia can fit the programme's global change themes; heat is not a named priority.

recipients.text: Researchers and institutions in APN member countries, usually in multi-country teams.

remit.text: Grants that strengthen national institutions, country programming and direct access entities, requested through the National Designated Authority.

relevance.label: related
relevance.why: Countries can use readiness support to plan adaptation, including heat-health and early-warning measures, where national priorities include them.

access_note.text: Requests come from the National Designated Authority, or an entity it nominates.

recipients.text: National Designated Authorities and direct access entities.

remit.text: Projects and programmes proposed by accredited entities, national or international.

relevance.label: related
relevance.why: Large adaptation programmes can include heat measures; heat is not a separate GCF window.

access_note.text: Only accredited entities submit funding proposals; national entities seek accreditation with a nomination from their National Designated Authority.

recipients.text: Accredited entities, national (direct access) or international.

remit.text: Grants of up to US$50,000 a project, averaging about US$25,000, to national community-based organisations and NGOs, aligned with each country's programme strategy.

relevance.label: potential
relevance.why: Community projects on greening, water or energy can reduce heat exposure where they fit the country programme strategy; heat is not a named priority.

access_note.text: Applicants contact the National Coordinator in their country for guidelines and forms; the programme charges no fee.

recipients.text: National community-based organisations and NGOs.

records.name: Adaptation Fund locally led adaptation (single-country grants)

remit.text: Grants for locally led adaptation projects, submitted through accredited implementing entities.

relevance.label: related
relevance.why: Locally led adaptation can include heat measures chosen by communities; the window is not heat-specific.

access_note.text: Proposals are submitted by implementing entities accredited to the Fund.

recipients.text: Accredited implementing entities, working with local actors.

records.name: Adaptation Fund Climate Innovation Accelerator calls (via CTCN)

remit.text: Technical assistance for climate adaptation innovations, by region.

relevance.label: related
relevance.why: Adaptation innovations for heat could apply; the calls cover adaptation broadly.

recipients.text: Applicants in the call's region, as each call defines.

remit.text: Research awards that make the health effects of climate change visible, with stakeholders engaged.

relevance.label: related
relevance.why: Heat-related health effects are within the scheme's scope of climate's effects on health.

recipients.text: Research teams; see the scheme page for eligibility.

remit.text: Research for climate adaptation and resilience, co-funded by IDRC and the UK.

relevance.label: related
relevance.why: Adaptation research on heat risk fits the programme's adaptation and resilience remit.

recipients.text: Research institutions, through competitive calls.

records.name: Advancing Research on Climate and Health

remit.text: Research on climate and health with the UK's FCDO.

relevance.label: related
relevance.why: Climate and health research includes heat-related illness and health systems.

recipients.text: Research institutions, through calls.

past_support.text: Grants from the global call for extreme heat solutions (2025), including grantees in South and Southeast Asia.

remit.text: Pooled philanthropic fund for adaptation and resilience; it ran a global call for extreme heat solutions.

relevance.label: explicit
relevance.why: Its global call funded extreme heat solutions, with grantees in South and Southeast Asia.

recipients.text: Organisations selected through calls.

remit.text: Philanthropic initiative on efficient, climate-friendly cooling.

relevance.label: explicit
relevance.why: Sustainable cooling is its whole remit.

access_note.text: No open call is listed; funding reaches partners it selects.

recipients.text: Partners it selects.

limits_note.text: Whether it accepts unsolicited proposals was not confirmed on its page.

remit.text: Grants for community-led, rights-based approaches to climate resilience.

relevance.label: potential
relevance.why: Community-led resilience work could address heat; the fund's priorities are set by its own process.

recipients.text: Organisations it invites.

records.name: Community Resilience Partnership Program Trust Fund

remit.text: Technical assistance and grant resources to scale up community-level climate adaptation, with a climate-poverty focus.

relevance.label: related
relevance.why: Community adaptation investments in ADB member countries can include heat measures.

access_note.text: Resources flow through ADB operations with member governments; there is no open call for organisations.

recipients.text: ADB developing member countries, through ADB projects.

records.name: ADB technical assistance: Investing in Resilience to Extreme Heat (59391-001)

remit.text: Regional technical assistance to integrate gender-responsive extreme heat adaptation into investments.

relevance.label: explicit
relevance.why: Extreme heat adaptation is the subject of the technical assistance.

access_note.text: Consultants are recruited through ADB's consulting system; governments take part through ADB operations.

recipients.text: ADB member countries, with consultants recruited for the work.

remit.text: Technical assistance that helps cities prepare climate-smart urban projects.

relevance.label: related
relevance.why: Cities can request help to prepare projects such as greening or heat-resilient infrastructure; heat is not a separate window.

access_note.text: Cities and their partners submit an expression of interest.

recipients.text: Cities and local governments, and organisations working with them.

remit.text: Funding released ahead of predicted shocks, through UN agencies.

relevance.label: related
relevance.why: Anticipatory frameworks can cover forecast heatwaves where agreed in advance.

access_note.text: Allocations go to UN agencies; organisations reach it only as their partners.

recipients.text: UN agencies.

remit.text: Rapid response funding for member organisations of the Start Network.

relevance.label: related
relevance.why: Members can raise alerts for heatwaves; heatwave responses have been funded.

access_note.text: Only Start Network members can raise alerts and receive funding.

recipients.text: Start Network member organisations.

remit.text: Fast funding for National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, including anticipatory action.

relevance.label: related
relevance.why: Anticipatory and response funding can be requested for heatwaves by National Societies.

access_note.text: Only National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies can request it.

recipients.text: National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.

records.name: UNICEF Venture Fund: climate and health

remit.text: Equity-free funding of up to US$100,000 for early-stage climate and health technology.

relevance.label: explicit
relevance.why: The 2026 call cited children's exposure to extreme heat among its concerns.

recipients.text: Early-stage technology companies, as each call defines.

remit.text: Annual challenge for resilience innovations across the Global South.

relevance.label: potential
relevance.why: Themes change each year; heat was not confirmed as a 2026 theme.

recipients.text: Innovators across the Global South.

past_support.text: An earlier Grand Challenges call on climate, health, agriculture and gender (closed).

records.name: Grand Challenges: climate change's impact on health, agriculture and gender

remit.text: A Grand Challenges call on solutions to climate change's impact on health, agriculture and gender, including heat stress in South Asia.

relevance.label: explicit
relevance.why: Heat stress, including in South Asia, was named in the call.

recipients.text: Applicants as each Grand Challenges call defines.

remit.text: A call for proposals on deploying sustainable cooling.

relevance.label: explicit
relevance.why: Sustainable cooling is the call's subject.

recipients.text: As defined by the call.

remit.text: Design grants that move blended-finance concepts for Southeast Asia towards investment.

relevance.label: potential
relevance.why: Its 2026 themes were climate-resilient agriculture and nature-based solutions; a heat-related design could fit where it matches them.

recipients.text: Proponents of blended-finance designs for Southeast Asia.

remit.text: Grants for ecosystem-based adaptation, in small-size and medium-size calls.

relevance.label: potential
relevance.why: Ecosystem-based measures such as urban greening can lower heat; the fund's priority countries and themes decide fit.

recipients.text: Organisations as each call defines.

remit.text: Grants to civil society organisations and collectives in Commonwealth member countries; climate and environmental justice is one priority.

relevance.label: potential
relevance.why: Civil society work on heat and climate justice could fit the climate and environmental justice priority.

recipients.text: Not-for-profit organisations and collectives in eligible Commonwealth countries.

remit.text: Grants for practitioners' exchange on common issues in Asia.

relevance.label: potential
relevance.why: Cross-border exchange on heat among practitioners could fit where heat is the common issue.

recipients.text: Teams in East and Southeast Asia, as each call defines.

records.name: Z Zurich Foundation partnership with the IFRC Global Climate Resilience Platform

remit.text: Partnership support for the IFRC's Global Climate Resilience Platform, which works on extreme heat.

relevance.label: explicit
relevance.why: The platform's report names extreme heat among its work.

access_note.text: No public application route was found; support flows through the IFRC partnership.

recipients.text: Through the IFRC and National Societies.

records.name: Horizon Europe Cluster 1: Health (environment and health topics)

remit.text: Research and innovation actions on environment and health, including climate-related exposures.

relevance.label: related
relevance.why: Climate-related exposures include heat; the topic encourages international cooperation.

access_note.text: Consortia apply through the Funding and Tenders portal; whether a partner from a given Asian country receives EU funding depends on Horizon Europe's list of countries eligible for funding.

recipients.text: Consortia; eligibility for funding of partners outside Europe depends on the programme's country list.
